paper.title: Discovering a Zero  (Zero-Vector Class of Machine Learning)

summary: Representative-dependent addition invalidates the central vector space and derived zero interpretation; finite uniform-noise training remains an empirical method. Bounded code variant/training-mode defects and NCE constant error identified.
limitations: No author program executed; no benchmarks or raw predictions reproduced.
Public commit is not authenticated as the exact historical experiment revision; BCE/CE and 50/100 epoch variants differ.
Remaining repository and ImageNet embedding implementation not exhaustively inspected.
Fresh independent AI check completed; scientific adjudication pending and no human review.

problems.title: Decision-equivalence addition is not well defined; derived vector-space claims fail
problems.location: Sections2-4 Eqs1,6-20 pp2-5; AppendixC pp13-14; AppendixF pp29-30
problems.evidence: Normalized p(.7,.3) and p_prime(.9,.1) are the same Eq1 class at threshold.5, yet their mixtures with q(.15,.85) classify opposite bins. Signed h and2h also give opposite sum decisions.
problems.assumptions: Two unit-volume bins and normalized positive densities; threshold rescaling allowed by paper. Signed logits independently allowed by S.
problems.counterevidence: AppendixA mixture identity is correct for fixed densities; paper acknowledges arbitrary-logit difficulty and calls zero derivations intuition. Finite-domain uniform noise remains valid.
problems.impact: Central real vector space, unique uniform additive-identity distribution and basis inference not established.
problems.repair: Replace quotient and claims or present finite-noise classification/Boolean indicator operations without false vector-space theorem.
problems.repair_verification: Exact fraction, signed-logit, mass-escape and tensor-cancellation checks; replacement theory unverified.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read physical pp.2-5 Eqs.(1),(6)-(20), pp.13-14 Eqs.(34)-(39), and pp.29-30 Eqs.(42)-(51) plus the explicit intuition disclaimer. Actually viewed source pp.2,5,29 to confirm typography. Eq.(1) includes the displayed positive rescaling family and a union with valid-logit set S; normalization constants are1 for the finite-density example.
independent_check.decisive_check: Take two unit-volume bins, p=(7/10,3/10),pprime=(9/10,1/10),q=(3/20,17/20),tau=1/2. Every density integrates to1 and pprime=2(p-tau)+tau. Their Eq.(6) equal mixtures are (17/40,23/40) and (21/40,19/40), giving opposite threshold regions. Thus changing an explicitly permitted representative changes the output decision class. At zero threshold h=(1,-1),hprime=2h,g=(-1.5,1.5) similarly gives sum signs(-,+) versus(+,-), with no equality-boundary ambiguity. Eq.(12) also makes2[h]=[h] atzero threshold, which by cancellation is impossible for a nonzero vector in a real vector space.
independent_check.counterevidence: The fixed-density equal-mixture identity in AppendixA is valid. It does not resolve operation independence on equivalence classes. Page3 acknowledges arbitrary-logit merging fails; introducing sets without changing representative addition does not remove that failure. A selected canonical density or a new threshold rule is additional structure, not an established repair. Boolean indicator operations can be valid independently. AppendixF retains addition and includes positive scaling, so its strictly increasing part already retains the counterexample; allowing constant nondecreasing transforms further loses decision preservation. Both p.5 and p.30 disclaim a formal uniform-zero proof, and these qualifications are preserved.
independent_check.dependent_claim_checks: For any normalized r, epsilon*r tends tozero but normalizes back tor, so the normalization limit does not identify a unique density. Uniform on[-R,R] has mass1 in total but mass1/R in[-1,1], hence no uniform probability limit onR. Finite image boxes remain valid sampling domains. AppendixF monotone equivalence identifies x andx^3 at threshold0 via cube/cube-root, so its class basis cannot use both as independent elements. Independently of any quotient convention, ordered m12=1,m21=-1 cancels x1*x2-x2*x1 identically in Eq.(35)/(39); symmetric multiindices would remove this coefficient redundancy but not establish universal analytic expansion.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Major retained for the central vector-space and derived additive-identity/basis claims. Local normalization or coefficient repairs cannot fix the representative dependence. Replace the theory or narrow it to finite-noise classification and Boolean operations. No replacement vector space or repaired empirical model was verified, and no conclusion that finite uniform-noise training fails is drawn.

problems.title: Two-output CE repository variant compares arbitrary raw logit offsets
problems.evidence: A(0,2),B(0,1) chooses A; shift Bto(10,11) chooses B with identical Bsoftmax/loss.
problems.assumptions: Two-output CE variant, final common bias free; not one-output BCE.
problems.counterevidence: MNIST repository notebook specifies BCE; grouped JamesWeb uses softmax; exact figures historical configuration unverified.
problems.impact: Released CE combination is not invariant to individually equivalent classifiers; does not prove reported accuracies false.
problems.repair: Use calibrated log-odds/probability route and authenticate executed variant.
problems.repair_verification: Additive-offset removal algebraically justified; empirical repair not run.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read repository_zero.py:74-89 two-output FullyConnectedNet, CE loss, SGD without additional offset penalty; Curiosity.py:21-30 evaluates each model then compares logits[:,-1]. The last Linear layer has an unconstrained bias.
independent_check.decisive_check: CE(z+c*1,y)=-z_y-c+log(sum exp(z_i+c))=CE(z,y), and softmax is unchanged. For A=(0,2),B=(0,1), the last-logit selector chooses A; B+(10,10)=(10,11) changes its choice toB while its positive probability remains exp(1)/(1+exp(1))=.7310585786 and loss .3132616875. A common final bias shift realizes this for all inputs. Training on uniform noise does not remove this invariance in the inspected unpenalized CE route.
independent_check.counterevidence: MNIST_repository_source_cells.txt specifies one output and BCEWithLogitsLoss; the common two-output shift argument does not apply there. Its number_of_non_zero_classes=1 also does not match the current helper binary branch==0, so historical execution remains uncertain. JamesWeb.py:38-54 uses softmax and masks a noise-class win; it is invariant to the same additive shift. No blanket claim about Figures41-44 or accuracy validity is retained.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor bounded release defect because independently equivalent CE models can receive different combined decisions. Margins/probabilities remove additive-offset ambiguity, but cross-model priors, noise and calibration still require validation. No author-model fix or benchmark recomputation performed.

problems.title: Trainer fails to restore model training mode after epoch evaluation
problems.evidence: No self.model.train call; self.model.eval at107,129,159. Independent public-framework probe batch counter1 remains1in eval, becomes2aftertrain restoration.
problems.assumptions: New model starts train mode and standard helper loop used; CIFAR architecture has mode-sensitive layers.
problems.counterevidence: Both baseline/method sharehelper; linearReLU MNIST lacks same consequence; historical notebook100epochs vs script/figure50 not authenticated.
problems.impact: Later CIFAR epochs optimize with dropout disabled and frozen running BN statistics; benchmark magnitude unknown.
problems.repair: Call model.train at training-epoch entry; re-evaluate affected runs.
problems.repair_verification: Independent mode semantics checked; author code not run.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read the entire zeroTrainer class and relevant network definitions. ZeroTrainer.train is a wrapper loop, not nn.Module.train; _run_epoch calls _epoch_train before _epoch_test/_epoch_pf/_epoch_of. No self.model.train restoration is present. CIFAR AllClassVGGNet and ClassWiseVGGNet use active BatchNorm and Dropout, whereas MNIST FullyConnectedNet is Linear/ReLU.
independent_check.decisive_check: After _epoch_test line107 calls model.eval, standard Module.eval sets self.training=False recursively and leaves it false; .to(device), optimizer.zero_grad,backward andstep do not change mode. Every later _epoch_train therefore runs with frozen BatchNorm running-stat updates and disabled Dropout. Gradients still exist. This control-flow derivation agrees with the frozen independent public-framework counter sequence1,1,2 when training mode is explicitly restored; that actual earlier probe is reused, not represented as a new execution.
independent_check.counterevidence: Both compared CIFAR models share the helper; neither direction nor size of relative accuracy change follows without a repaired run. Linear/ReLU MNIST lacks this same mode-sensitive effect. Script/figure50 versus notebook100 epochs and unknown historical code remain material limitations. No evidence that all training or gradients stop.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor implementation issue scoped to mode-sensitive models and this training path, not a demonstrated failure of historical plots. Restore model.train at each optimization epoch entry, then rerun affected protocols to quantify impact; only restoration semantics, not empirical results, verified.

problems.title: Noise-contrastive density formula substitutes k for log(k)
problems.evidence: p_n=k requires G=logpd-logk and pd=kexpG; pd.4,k.25 printedreconstruction2.05444.
problems.assumptions: k has explicit density meaning; equal priors as Eq26.
problems.counterevidence: Could be repaired by redefining a logconstant; score Eq29 unaffected.
problems.impact: Absolute density normalization wrong, no demonstrated empirical score failure.
problems.repair: Correct logarithm and state sampling-prior factor.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read pp.8-9 Eqs.(26)-(29) and actually viewed p.8: pn(u)=k explicitly denotes noise density, not its logarithm. The displayed log-odds corresponds to equal sampling priors.
independent_check.decisive_check: Substitution gives G=log(pd)-log(k), therefore pd=k*exp(G). With pd=.4,k=.25,exp(G)=1.6 and G=.4700036292; the printed exp(G+k)=1.6*exp(.25)=2.0544406667 rather than .4. For unequal class priors Bayes odds additionally contains log(pi_d/pi_n), requiring the inverse prior ratio in density reconstruction.
independent_check.counterevidence: Redefining the symbol as a log-density constant can repair the local notation but contradicts its current explicit definition. Spatial derivatives of either constant vanish, so Eq.(29) score is unchanged. Uniform noise on a finite box and equal priors gives a pd>1/V superlevel decision set, not a general theorem recovering full support or an unseen class complement.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor algebraic density normalization error with a verified correction, no demonstrated score-gradient or historical generation failure. Correct log(k), state priors and finite support; no author inference pipeline was executed.

Ordered Taylor coefficients admit nonzero cancellation.
Two-output CE raw-logit shift preserves individual loss but flips repository choice; one-output BCE and JamesWeb excluded.
Trainer mode-call AST and independent public-framework BatchNorm/Dropout probe.
NCE constant correction preserves score gradient.
Noise draws and accuracy/purity loader separation; all44sourcefigures actually viewed.
